newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank of Portugal sees no inflationary pressures.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Portugal sees no inflationary pressures.

text.p: Senior Bank of Portugal officials said there was no sign of inflationary pressures in the Portuguese economy before the end of 1998 because economic growth was still below historical potential.

In its latest quarterly report the Bank had forecast economic growth of 3.0-3.75 percent for 1997. A higher outcome would only be possible if the European Union (EU) grew faster than expected, governor Antonio de Sousa told a news conference.

He said EU growth was one explanation for the better than initially predicted economic performance in 1996 when the Bank says gross domestic product (GDP) expanded 3.3 percent, sharply above its 2.5 percent forecast.
"We see a slight acceleration in 1997 (but) more than that will depend on what happens in the European Union," he told a news conference.

Deputy governor Luis Campos e Cunha said that private consumption could pick up slightly from the 2.8 percent recorded in 1997 while public consumption was seen rising to two percent from one percent last year.
He said that the stability of the escudo and international prices as well as salary moderation were helping to maintain the deflationary process.
The Bank officials declined to make any forecast for the year-on-year inflation rate in the coming months when analysts say it could drop below two percent from 2.5 percent in March.
However, de Sousa noted that the impact of meat prices on the index last year in April and May, when the mad cow disease scare was at its height, was around 0.7-0.8 percentage points.
